key_insight: Random train/test splits overestimate machine-learning performance on perovskite photovoltaic data because they leak duplicated recipes, so grouped evaluation is needed to measure true generalisation.
engineering_relevance: The proposed provenance-grouped protocol gives device engineers a more realistic benchmark for selecting models that can predict new perovskite designs, institutions, and future discoveries.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits that separate duplicates, publications, and institutions.
Benchmarked 13 models across increasingly strict evaluation regimes.
evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another, and model rankings shift sharply from random splits to unseen-institution and future-discovery splits.
watch_item: Results from random-split benchmarks should not be treated as evidence of physical generalisation, especially when duplicated or near-duplicated device recipes are present.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
